summary: Independent review of submission sub-mv15wpmr-015f7530 (brief.md sha256 9b47c253...). All 37 user requirement ids (RS-01..RS-33, RS-NF-1..4) are present and unweakened (RS-NF-1..4 carried as NFR1..4 because the engine's criterion parser /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-?\d+$/ rejects two-hyphen ids; verified against lib/gates.js:197). Fixture arithmetic verified (A+B = 8400, A+E = 9500). Six major findings block approval: the fixture does not pin inventory, so under the brief's own multiplicity rule the exact planner contradicts RS-06/RS-11 if any supplier holds two bundles; the payment state machine has no provider PENDING states and the aggregate rescue status derivation is unspecified; the execute claim, reservation-expiry race and authorization lifecycle on non-capture outcomes are unspecified; simulation labelling omits Sandbox transactions and demo data; the deterministic test layout conflicts with the no-network clause of NFR1 (Playwright browser download); and the live-PayPal variant of RS-31/32 was dropped rather than marked Unverified. No reviewer-directed text found in the brief. Checks were run by the reviewer with node -e but could not be recorded through `eccode evidence run` because the PreToolUse identity guard refused --actor architecture-reviewer from this dispatch (agent_type general-purpose); their programs are reproduced in the findings.

criteria.description: Equivalent Arabic and English requests (RS-FIX-1 wording) yield identical core fields. [D fake; LM real]
criteria.notes: Decidable: equality on normalised fields with fake and real provider; AI feature statement gives thresholds (>= 90 % field match on text).

criteria.description: A clear package image yields capacity/diameter with provenance image. [D fake; LM real]
An ambiguous image yields unknown fields plus a clarification question and no invented numeric value. [D fake; LM real]
Missing budget/deadline: approve and paypal/create return 409 MISSING_BUDGET/MISSING_DEADLINE; no reservation or payment operation. [D]
Injection strings end as data; no permission, amount, supplier, plan version or role differs from the control run. [D; LM]
criteria.notes: Trust boundary (2) states model output is schema-validated data with no tools; control-run comparison is decidable.

criteria.description: Canonical RS-FIX-1 returns A+B, 8400 cents, 2 pickups, ready 10:30. [D]
criteria.notes: Arithmetic verified (3000+1000+3600+800 = 8400, ready max(10:00,10:30) = 10:30). Not decidable as written: the fixture does not state on_hand per supplier, and the adopted planner enumerates multiplicities 0..ceil(N/qty) per offer; with A holding 2 bundles the exact optimum is A x2 = 7000 cents, 1 pickup, ready 10:00 (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: Supplier C rejected with INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER. [D]
criteria.notes: Brute-force check: C's bundle carries exactly this code (cups 90 mm, lids 95 mm).

criteria.description: Supplier D rejected with READY_AFTER_DEADLINE. [D]
With B removed the best plan is A+E at 9500 cents. [D]

criteria.description: With B removed and budget 9000: no plan, OVER_BUDGET listed, at least one suggestion. [D]
criteria.notes: Decidable. Brute force confirms no feasible plan; valid relaxations are budget -> 9500 (A+E) and deadline -> 11:20 (D at 8000); 'more pickups' yields no plan even at 3 pickups, so the AC's example list contains an invalid suggestion (ARCH-7, minor).

criteria.description: With max pickups = 1 the canonical scenario is infeasible with TOO_MANY_PICKUPS/INSUFFICIENT_QTY explanations. [D]
criteria.notes: Infeasibility verified only under one-bundle-per-supplier inventory; INSUFFICIENT_QTY for A alone presupposes A cannot supply two bundles, which the fixture does not state (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: Under-quantity plans are never feasible; approval of a tampered plan body is refused with 409. [D]

criteria.description: Offer price change supersedes the approved version; reserve/execute on the old version refused. [D]
criteria.notes: Plan-side behaviour is decidable, but the fate of reservations and PayPal authorizations already taken against the superseded version is unspecified (ARCH-3).

criteria.description: Two OS processes reserve the last bundle; exactly one active, the other OUT_OF_STOCK; reserved <= on_hand. [D multi-process]
criteria.notes: Conditional UPDATE reserved + q <= on_hand inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus CHECK constraint is a sound cross-process guard with node:sqlite WAL (RISK-4).

criteria.description: Expired reservation released exactly once; one ledger row; second pass no-op. [D]
criteria.notes: Decidable. The expiry-vs-execute race is raised separately (ARCH-3 b).

criteria.description: Same Idempotency-Key -> same reservation id, no second reservation or ledger row. [D]

criteria.description: Supplier refusal -> order refused, customer sees refusal with next step, new plan version excluding that supplier. [D; B]
criteria.notes: Replanning is specified; what happens to the refused order's authorization and to the other suppliers' authorizations/reservation items is not (ARCH-3 c).

criteria.description: Cancel URL leaves the operation voided/created, no capture row, execute refuses. [D fake; LP]
criteria.notes: Return-URL ownership and idempotent authorize are not covered (ARCH-10, minor).

criteria.description: Client-supplied amount/currency/supplier ignored; PayPal order amount equals the server-approved total. [D; LP]
criteria.notes: Trust boundary (1): server derives amount from the approved plan version.

criteria.description: N concurrent/repeated execute -> exactly one capture per supplier order (operation key unique, PayPal-Request-Id reused). [D fake; LP]
criteria.notes: The invariants (unique key, intent persisted first, state machine) are right, but the brief never says how concurrent executors are serialised before the first external call; the capture row's key must be deterministic per supplier order and its INSERT must be the claim (ARCH-3 a).

criteria.description: One authorization failure -> no capture on any supplier order; plan non_executable with reason. [D]
criteria.notes: No-capture is decidable; the brief does not say the successful authorizations are voided, so the honest end state of those operations is undefined (ARCH-3 c).

criteria.description: Capture fails on the second supplier: first capture refunded, uncaptured authorizations voided, statuses refund_requested -> refund_pending -> refunded|refund_failed, reservation reconciling, handover blocked. [D fake faults]
criteria.notes: Decidable for the fault 'capture fails'; not for the real provider outcome 'capture PENDING' or 'authorization PENDING', for which the state machine has no state (ARCH-2).

criteria.description: Same webhook (transmission id) delivered twice applies once. [D; LP]
criteria.notes: transmission_id UNIQUE; live variant depends on Q6/A10 polling fallback.

criteria.description: Invalid webhook signature -> 4xx, signature_status invalid, no transition. [D; LP]
criteria.notes: Raw body retained for verify-webhook-signature (docs/integration-research.md, marked verify).

Kill/restart mid-saga preserves orders, payment operations and recovery progress; reconciler completes the saga. [D]
criteria.notes: Intent persisted before every call; in-process reconciler with persisted progress.

criteria.description: Customer X requesting customer Y's request/order gets 404/403 and no data. [D]
Supplier A patching supplier B's inventory -> 403, B unchanged. [D]
Scan of assets, responses, logs, screenshots, submission files finds no client id/secret; config redacts secrets. [D scan; I]

Browser journey at 360/1280 px request -> ... -> collection with screenshots. [B]
criteria.notes: The goal's RS-31 says 'PayPal approvals'; the brief narrows it to '(fake adapter page)' with no live/user-run variant, instead of marking the live journey Unverified with its blocker as goal.md prescribes (ARCH-6).

criteria.notes: Same narrowing as RS-31 (ARCH-6); also depends on the authorization lifecycle on supersession (ARCH-3 c).

Fake-adapter payloads carry simulated: true; UI shows provider badges and a persistent banner while a fake adapter is active. [D; B]

Plan, reservation, payment operation and fulfilment statuses persisted separately; rescue status computed, no stored column. [D; I]
criteria.notes: Absence of a stored column is decidable; correctness of the derivation is not, because the brief never defines how the goal's aggregate states (plan_found ... collected, cancelling, refunding, failed_needs_attention) derive from the four machines (ARCH-2).

criteria.description: Admin reset 409 while any payment operation is authorized|captured|refund_pending|unknown; forced reset records a reason and archives. [D]
UPDATE/DELETE on audit_events or inventory_ledger fails; every reservation/release/consume writes a ledger row. [D]
Upload rejects > 5 MB and non-PNG/JPEG/WebP; random stored name; deletion with the request verified. [D]

criteria.notes: If npm test includes the [B] Playwright suites, a clean clone needs the Chromium download (network beyond npm). The brief relies on Chromium being 'pre-installed' in this environment, which does not hold for a judge's clone (ARCH-5).

npm test, npm run test:live-model (RS_LIVE_MODEL=1) and npm run test:live-paypal (RS_LIVE_PAYPAL=1) are separate, labelled scripts. [I]

Planner on RS-FIX-1 and random catalogs <= 12 offers < 1 s; deterministic suite < 5 min offline. [D timing]

criteria.description: Every response and log line carries requestId; live model run cost reported and <= USD 1. [D; LM report]
criteria.notes: Requirements text also says logs never contain secrets or raw PayPal payloads; the AC does not test it (ARCH-9, minor).

criteria.description: Users, problem, workflows, constraints, scope boundaries and non-obvious requirements (authz, retention, error handling, accessibility, observability, abuse, cost) are explicit.
criteria.notes: Strong on users/scope/workflows. Gaps: aggregate status derivation and PENDING states (ARCH-2), authorization lifecycle on non-capture outcomes (ARCH-3), Sandbox/demo-data labelling (ARCH-4), runtime model-cost/abuse limits (ARCH-11), return-URL handling (ARCH-10).

criteria.description: Each acceptance criterion is decidable by a test or inspection and every requirement traces to a criterion.
criteria.notes: 1:1 id traceability verified for all 37 user ids. Not decidable as written: RS-06/09/11 (inventory not pinned, ARCH-1), RS-36 (derivation, ARCH-2), NFR1/NFR3 (browser suite placement, ARCH-5); NFR5/NFR6 requirement text exceeds the AC (ARCH-9).

criteria.description: Risky or false assumptions identified; design-blocking open questions routed to the user.
criteria.notes: A1-A10 are stated and reversible; environment facts (A6-A8) match docs/integration-research.md and docs/build/state.md. A2 (credential-per-merchant) is unverified against PayPal's primary docs and its single-credential fallback changes what RS-22 exercises (ARCH-18). Q1/Q3/Q6 have working defaults, so design need not wait (ARCH-15).

criteria.description: No component is unnecessary for the stated requirements; no simpler design works.
criteria.notes: Single process, SQLite, fake adapters and the exact planner with oracle are each justified against alternatives. The model-rephrased explanations (ai/explain.js) are the one optional component: a second paid call and injection surface for no required outcome (ARCH-13, minor).

criteria.description: Technology limits, rate limits, latency and cost are accounted for.
criteria.notes: Node 22.22 / node:sqlite / CLI model route are verified here; PayPal facts are search-engine summaries marked verify in docs/integration-research.md (paypal.com and devpost.com unreachable; this reviewer did not check them either). The clean-clone NFR1 claim is not feasible as laid out if browser tests sit inside npm test (ARCH-5). Planner space at 12 offers with multiplicity is small enough for exactness (< 3^12 nodes).

criteria.description: Trust boundaries, secrets, PII, prompt injection and least privilege are addressed.
criteria.notes: Four trust boundaries, RBAC default-deny, server-derived amounts, hosted approval link, webhook verification and raw-body retention, append-only ledgers, env-only secrets. Minor gaps: return-URL token ownership (ARCH-10), magic-byte MIME check (ARCH-17), runtime abuse/cost limits on paid model calls (ARCH-11). No reviewer-directed directives found in the brief.

criteria.description: AI adds real value; evaluation cases with thresholds, fallback and human oversight exist.
criteria.notes: Value is confined to extraction; everything downstream is deterministic. Eval set (>= 10 bilingual, >= 6 images) with thresholds, human confirmation of every field, fake provider and cost caps are present. The runtime degraded path when the model fails should be stated (ARCH-12, minor).

criteria.description: Every material risk has likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner.
criteria.notes: RISK-1..12 complete. Missing entries: authorization hold/expiry window (unverified 3-day honour / 29-day validity) and Playwright browser download on clean clones (ARCH-16, info).

findings.title: RS-FIX-1 does not pin inventory, so the exact planner's expected results are undecidable
findings.detail: The Architecture section adopts docs/build/plan.md section 5 unchanged: candidates are enumerated with multiplicity 0..ceil(N/qty) per offer and availability = on_hand - reserved. Neither the brief's fixture reference nor goal.md's RS-FIX-1 table states on_hand for suppliers A-E. The reviewer ran a brute-force lexicographic solver over the fixture (node -e; program: five offers with price/fee/ready/compatibility from the table, N = 200, deadline 11:00, budget 12000, max 2 pickups, objective (total, pickups, ready)). With one bundle on hand per supplier it reproduces every expected outcome: A+B 8400/2 pickups/10:30, C INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER, D READY_AFTER_DEADLINE, without B A+E 9500, without B at 9000 no plan, max 1 pickup no plan with INSUFFICIENT_QTY on A/B/E alone. With A at on_hand = 2 bundles the same exact planner returns A x2 = 7000 cents, 1 pickup, ready 10:00, which contradicts RS-06 and makes RS-11 feasible. Exactness and RS-06/09/11 therefore hold only under an unstated inventory assumption, and the oracle property test (<= 6 offers) as described does not exercise multiplicity > 1.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief's fixture (or an explicit RS-FIX-1 addendum it cites) states on_hand per supplier (A, B, E: exactly one bundle; C, D: one bundle), RS-06/09/11 reference that inventory, the RS-14 'last bundle' wording is tied to it, and the oracle property test is required to include catalogs where on_hand >= 2 bundles so multiplicity is covered.

findings.title: Honest-status rule not fully specified: no provider PENDING states and no aggregate derivation
findings.detail: goal.md's 'Honest statuses' names the payment operation machine created -> approved -> authorized -> captured | voided | authorization_failed plus refund states and unknown, and an aggregate rescue status with cancelling | refunding | failed_needs_attention that is derived, never stored. docs/integration-research.md records that PayPal returns authorization status PENDING and capture status PENDING (and DECLINED) as normal outcomes. The brief's workflows and RS-22 have no state for a pending authorization or pending capture: such an outcome would have to be shown as authorized/captured (false), as failed (false) or as unknown (which the brief reserves for lost responses and which the reconciler would then 'resolve' from a provider state that is still pending). The brief also never defines how the aggregate rescue status is computed from the four machines; RS-36 only asserts that no stored column exists, so an implementation that reports purchase_confirmed while a supplier order is refused or a refund is pending would pass RS-36. The word 'refunding' and 'failed_needs_attention' do not occur in the brief.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when (a) the payment-operation machine gains explicit pending states (e.g. authorization_pending, capture_pending) with their allowed transitions, reconciler polling and the rule that capture never proceeds from authorization_pending, and RS-22/RS-25 ACs name them; (b) the brief contains a derivation table mapping combinations of plan/reservation/payment/fulfilment states to each aggregate state in goal.md (plan_found ... collected, cancelling, refunding, failed_needs_attention), with precedence rules; (c) RS-36's AC adds at least three derivation assertions (any refund_requested/refund_pending -> refunding; any refused or non_executable with no compensation left -> failed_needs_attention or cancelling as defined; collected only when every supplier order is collected and every capture is captured).

findings.title: Execute claim, reservation-expiry race and authorization lifecycle on non-capture outcomes are unspecified
findings.detail: (a) RS-20 relies on 'operation key unique' and 'intent persisted before every call', but the capture operation row is created inside the saga. Two concurrent execute requests (or two processes, since RS-14 already requires multi-process correctness) can both read 'all authorized', both persist a capture intent and both call the provider unless the capture row's operation_key is deterministic per (plan version, supplier order, kind) and its INSERT in a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction is the claim, or the plan version takes an exclusive approved -> executing transition first. Relying on PayPal-Request-Id dedupe is not sufficient: docs/integration-research.md marks its retention (~6 h) as unverified and the fake adapter has no such dedupe. (b) The expiry job 'releases exactly once' and the saga 'revalidates reservation active' before capture, but nothing prevents expiry between revalidation and capture, producing a captured payment for released stock; the reservation only becomes reconciling on compensation. (c) Void of authorizations is defined only for the capture-phase failure. For RS-21 (one authorization failed: the other authorizations stay open), RS-17 (supplier refused after authorization), RS-13 (plan superseded after authorization) and reservation expiry, the brief does not say the outstanding authorizations are voided, what status their payment operations end in, or what the buyer sees; held funds would linger for the authorization validity window, which the research also marks unverified.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief (Main Workflows 6 and the ACs) states: the exclusive claim mechanism for execute (deterministic capture operation_key per supplier order inserted as the claim inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, or plan approved -> executing transition), and RS-20 is extended to two OS processes; that the execute transaction moves the reservation active -> consumed (or stamps an in-flight marker the expiry job must respect) before the first capture call, with an AC that an expiry pass during execution is a no-op; and the authorization lifecycle for every terminal non-capture outcome (RS-13 supersession, RS-17 refusal, RS-21 authorization failure, reservation expiry, RS-18 cancel): void all outstanding authorizations, resulting status voided, buyer-visible next step, with those assertions added to RS-13/17/21.

findings.title: Labelling requirement narrowed: Sandbox transactions and demonstration data are not covered by RS-34
findings.detail: goal.md (Version-one scope) requires: 'All demonstration data, simulations, test providers and Sandbox transactions are labelled in the UI and the API'. The brief's RS-34 and its AC label only fake adapters ('API payloads from fake adapters carry simulated: true; ... banner while a fake adapter is active'). Real Sandbox payments, the seeded suppliers A-E and their 'test prices, not market prices' are demonstration elements the goal wants labelled and the brief leaves unlabelled. This is a weakened mandatory scope statement rather than a dropped id, hence major rather than blocking.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-34 and its AC also require: every payment payload and UI element from the real adapter carries provider: 'paypal-sandbox' and a visible 'Sandbox: no real money' badge; seeded suppliers, offers and prices carry a demonstration flag rendered in the UI with the goal's 'test prices, not market prices' note; the AC is tested [D; B] for both adapters.

findings.title: Test-script layout makes NFR1 unfalsifiable or failing on a clean clone
findings.detail: NFR1's AC says a clean clone runs npm test with no network beyond npm. NFR3 defines three scripts (npm test, test:live-model, test:live-paypal) and the [B] Playwright suites (RS-31..33, NFR2, RS-17/34/35) are not assigned to any of them. If they run under npm test, a clean clone must download Chromium from Playwright's CDN, which is network beyond npm; the brief's Constraints only note that Chromium is pre-installed in this build environment, which a judge's machine will not have. If they run elsewhere, NFR3's script list is incomplete and NFR1 does not say which script is the deterministic one.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR1/NFR3 define the script layout: npm test = deterministic node --test only (offline after npm install, no browser); npm run test:browser = Playwright suites with the one-time documented browser install step named in the README; live scripts as already listed; and NFR1's AC is phrased against npm test alone while NFR2/RS-31..33 name test:browser.

findings.title: Live PayPal variant of the complete journeys dropped instead of marked Unverified
findings.detail: goal.md RS-31 reads 'PayPal approvals' and its preamble says that where a criterion depends on an external integration this environment cannot reach, the evidence table says Unverified with the exact blocker. The brief's RS-31 rewrites the step as 'PayPal approvals (fake adapter page)' and lists [B] only; RS-32 likewise. The Success Criteria extend live Sandbox evidence only to RS-18..RS-26. For a PayPal hackathon the end-to-end journey through the hosted Sandbox approval page is the central demonstration; removing it from the criteria (rather than keeping it as a user-run, Unverified-until-run variant) weakens a mandatory journey requirement.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when RS-31 and RS-32 each carry two variants: [B fake] deterministic in this environment, and [LP, user-run] through the real Sandbox hosted approval page with screenshots, recorded as Unverified with the blocker (A6/Q2) until the user runs it; and the Success Criteria/demo-video plan state that the submitted video uses the Sandbox page, not the fake adapter page.

findings.title: RS-10 example suggestions include a relaxation that does not produce a plan
findings.detail: RS-10's AC accepts 'raise budget to 9500, allow later ready time, or more pickups'. The reviewer's brute-force check for the B-removed, budget-9000 scenario shows: budget -> 9500 yields A+E (9500); deadline -> 11:20 yields D alone at 8000 cents; raising max pickups to 3 still yields no plan (every combination within budget is below 200 units or late). A planner emitting 'more pickups' here would pass the AC while giving the buyer wrong advice.
findings.recommendation: Require that suggestions are computed relaxations, each naming the relaxed constraint and the plan/total it yields (budget 9500 -> A+E; deadline 11:20 -> D at 8000); remove 'more pickups' from the RS-10 example list.

findings.title: RS-NF-1..4 carried as NFR1..4: forced by the engine, but traceability must follow the ids everywhere
findings.detail: The brief says the gate's parser accepts one hyphen per id. Verified: lib/gates.js:197 CRITERION_ID = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-?\d+$/ matches RS-01 and NFR1 and rejects RS-NF-1, so the alias is necessary, the user's id is preserved in parentheses and the four texts are semantically unchanged (checked side by side). Because the engine's required-criteria list, later gate reviews and the verification gate will show only NFR1..4, the user's ids can silently disappear from downstream artifacts.
findings.recommendation: Keep the alias; add the mapping line NFR1..4 = RS-NF-1..4 to docs/build/evidence.md and the acceptance report template, and have the design's criteria list repeat the parenthetical ids.

findings.title: NFR5/NFR6 requirement text promises more than their acceptance criteria test
findings.detail: Requirements: NFR5 includes 'API p95 < 300 ms on the deterministic suite' and NFR6 includes 'logs never contain secrets or raw card/PayPal payloads beyond ids'; the Acceptance Criteria for NFR5 and NFR6 omit both, so those clauses are untested requirements.
findings.recommendation: Either add the p95 timing and the log-content scan to the NFR5/NFR6 ACs (the latter can share the RS-29 scan) or remove the clauses from the requirement text.

findings.title: Return-URL handling: token ownership and idempotent authorize are unspecified
findings.detail: Workflow 4 authorizes on GET /api/paypal/return?token=. The brief does not say that the token must resolve to a payment operation in created/approved owned by the session's customer, nor that a repeated return hit (browser refresh, back button) performs at most one authorize call; RS-20 covers capture only.
findings.recommendation: State that the return handler looks the token up by provider_order_id scoped to the session's customer (404 otherwise) and that authorize is an idempotent operation keyed per supplier order; add a repeated-return assertion to RS-18 or RS-20.

findings.title: Runtime cost and abuse limits on paid model calls are not specified
findings.detail: NFR6's cost ceiling applies to the live test suite; extract and image upload are customer-triggered paid model calls at runtime with per-call budget caps only. A single customer looping extract can spend without bound and no rate limit is mentioned (the word 'rate limit' does not occur in the brief).
findings.recommendation: Add a config-level daily model budget (e.g. RS_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD) after which the provider refuses with a labelled error, and a per-session rate limit on extract/image, with a deterministic AC.

findings.title: Runtime degraded path when the model fails is not stated; eval corpus location unspecified
findings.detail: The AI feature statement covers test doubles, caps and thresholds, but not what the customer experiences when the real provider times out or returns schema-invalid output at runtime (the fake provider is a test double, not a fallback). The labelled evaluation set (>= 10 requests, >= 6 images) has no stated location or versioning.
findings.recommendation: State the degraded path (extraction row schema_ok = false, all fields unknown with provenance manual, the confirmation form lets the buyer enter every field, journey continues) and commit the eval corpus under a named path in the repository.

findings.title: Model-rephrased explanations add cost and injection surface for no required outcome
findings.detail: ai/explain.js lets the model rephrase planner-trace explanations. No RS id requires it, it is a second paid call per plan, and catalog text (an RS-05 injection vector) flows into that prompt.
findings.recommendation: Render explanations deterministically from the trace by default; if model rephrasing is kept, make it opt-in, labelled, and covered by the RS-05 control-run comparison.

findings.title: Idempotency details to pin in design
findings.detail: Same Idempotency-Key with a different body (another plan version) should be refused (422), not replayed. docs/integration-research.md says PayPal-Request-Id must be unique per call type and proposes <operationKey>:<kind>, while the brief says PayPal-Request-Id = operation key; consistent only because each kind has its own payment_operations row and key. The 6-hour retention (unverified) means the database-level idempotency and reconciler-before-retry, not PayPal, are the real double-capture guard, which the brief already states.
findings.recommendation: Record both points explicitly in the design's interface contracts.

findings.title: Design-blocking open questions have workable defaults; record them as decisions
findings.detail: Q1 (credentials), Q3 (model/spend) and Q6 (webhook URL) block design but the brief already states defaults (A2 single-credential fallback, haiku with USD 1 ceiling, polling fallback A10). Q8 (English-only UI) is answered by the goal.
findings.recommendation: Record the defaults with eccode decision add so the design gate proceeds, and keep Q1/Q3/Q6 open for the user to override.

findings.title: Risk register gaps
findings.detail: No entry for the authorization hold/expiry window (3-day honour, 29-day validity, both unverified in docs/integration-research.md) during the supplier-confirmation wait, nor for the Playwright browser download on clean clones (ARCH-5).
findings.recommendation: Add RISK-13 (authorization expiry before capture: re-read expiration_time, void and re-authorize path) and RISK-14 (browser install on judge machines) with owners.

findings.title: Upload type check should use magic bytes and verify ownership
findings.detail: RS-39 rejects non-PNG/JPEG/WebP but does not say whether by declared content type or by file signature; a declared image/png with arbitrary bytes would pass a header check. Upload is bound to a request id; the AC does not assert that only the owning customer can attach (RS-27 covers reads).
findings.recommendation: Specify magic-byte detection and an owner check in RS-39.

findings.title: Credential-per-merchant is unverified and its single-credential fallback changes what RS-22 exercises
findings.detail: A2 is reasonable (each supplier order is created and refunded with that supplier's own Sandbox app, so the payee is the caller) but rests on search-engine summaries marked verify in docs/integration-research.md; the reviewer could not check paypal.com either. It also implies one buyer approval per supplier order, which the UI must announce before the journey. In the single-credential fallback, supplier 1's refund and supplier 2's capture hit the same account, so the live RS-22 run no longer demonstrates cross-merchant compensation.
findings.recommendation: State in A2 that the number of buyer approvals equals the number of supplier orders and is shown before approval starts; state which RS-18..26 live rows are weakened in single-credential mode and label them in the evidence table; keep the user's Q1 answer as the trigger to verify A2 against PayPal's primary documentation.
